Round 2: lesson now has both requests read before either saves, which is the case the doc describes.

RabbitMQ confirms: for routable messages the basic.ack comes "when a message has been accepted by all the queues"; for persistent messages in durable queues, "after persisting the message to disk". Nothing in that page ties acceptance to any external database outcome.

PostgreSQL tutorial 3.4: "if some failure occurs that prevents the transaction from completing, then none of the steps affect the database at all." ROLLBACK: "causes all the updates made by the transaction to be discarded" (that PostgreSQL transaction only). RabbitMQ confirms: a confirmed message has been "accepted by all the queues". See minor issue on a drop during COMMIT.

issues.text: New in round 2. If the connection drops while COMMIT is in flight, the client cannot tell whether the server committed; PostgreSQL rolls back only a transaction whose commit never reached it. The sentence states a rollback as certain for any drop during "finishing". Claim 8 itself says "the connection drops first".
issues.quote: If finishing fails, for example because the connection to PostgreSQL drops, PostgreSQL rolls the order's change back.
issues.fix: Write "for example because the connection to PostgreSQL drops before the commit reaches it".

issues.text: New in round 2, in the changed sentence. The situation now says the stage-3 publish would sit in a handler, which runs before SaveChangesAsync. The next paragraph then lists 'after SaveChangesAsync' as one of the places to choose. From the prereq, handlers always run before the save, so I cannot see how a publish in a handler could go after it without leaving the handler.
issues.quote: With the stage-3 dispatcher, that publish would sit in a handler, which also runs before `SaveChangesAsync`.
issues.fix: Add one clause to that sentence, e.g. '…before SaveChangesAsync; putting it after the save would mean moving it out of the handler, into CancelOrderAsync itself.'
